script:
intro V G u v
intro h_adj
have h_main : 2 ≤ G.chromaticNumber := by
  -- Use the fact that if there is an edge, the chromatic number must be at least 2.
  have h₁ : G.Adj u v := h_adj
  have h₂ : 2 ≤ G.chromaticNumber := by
    -- Use the property of the chromatic number for a graph with an edge.
    by_contra h
    -- If the chromatic number is not at least 2, it must be 0 or 1.
    have h₃ : G.chromaticNumber ≤ 1 := by linarith
    -- Use the fact that if the graph has an edge, its chromatic number cannot be 0 or 1.
    have h₄ : G.Adj u v := h₁
    have h₅ : G.chromaticNumber = 0 ∨ G.chromaticNumber = 1 := by
      omega
    cases h₅ with
    | inl h₅ =>
      -- If the chromatic number is 0, there are no edges.
      have h₆ : ¬G.Adj u v := by
        simp_all [SimpleGraph.not_adjacent_iff]
        <;> aesop
      exact absurd h₄ h₆
    | inr h₅ =>
      -- If the chromatic number is 1, all vertices must be the same color.
      have h₆ : u = v := by
        have h₆₁ : G.chromaticNumber = 1 := h₅
        have h₆₂ : ∀ (x y : V), x ∈ G.vertices → y ∈ G.vertices → G.Adj x y → x = y := by
          intro x y hx hy hxy
          have h₆₃ : G.chromaticNumber = 1 := h₅
          have h₆₄ : ∀ (x y : V), x ∈ G.vertices → y ∈ G.vertices → G.Adj x y → x = y := by
            intro x y hx hy hxy
            -- Use the fact that if the chromatic number is 1, all vertices must be the same color.
            have h₆₅ : ∀ (x y : V), x ∈ G.vertices → y ∈ G.vertices → G.Adj x y → x = y := by
              intro x y hx hy hxy
              -- Use the fact that if the chromatic number is 1, all vertices must be the same color.
              simp_all [SimpleGraph.chromaticNumber_eq_one_iff]
              <;> aesop
            exact h₆₅ x y hx hy hxy
          exact h₆₄ x y hx hy hxy
        have h₆₃ : u ∈ G.vertices := by
          apply SimpleGraph.mem_vertices.mpr
          exact ⟨u, by simp⟩
        have h₆₄ : v ∈ G.vertices := by
          apply SimpleGraph.mem_vertices.mpr
          exact ⟨v, by simp⟩
        have h₆₅ : G.Adj u v := h₁
        have h₆₆ : u = v := h₆₂ u v h₆₃ h₆₄ h₆₅
        exact h₆₆
      -- If u = v, then the graph cannot have an edge.
      simp_all [SimpleGraph.not_adjacent_iff]
      <;> aesop
  exact h₂
exact h_main

intro α f p q
have h_main_forward : (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p ∨ q x) → p ∨ ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x := by
  intro h
  by_cases hp : p
  · -- Case: p is true
    exact Or.inl hp
  · -- Case: p is false
    have h₂ : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, ¬p → q x := by
      filter_upwards [h] with x hx using by tauto
    have h₃ : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x := by
      -- Use the fact that if p is false, then for all x, p ∨ q x implies q x
      have h₄ : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x := by
        filter_upwards [h₂] with x hx using by tauto
      exact h₄
    exact Or.inr h₃

have h_main_backward : (p ∨ ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x) → (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p ∨ q x) := by
  intro h
  cases h with
  | inl hp =>
    -- Case: p is true
    have h₁ : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p ∨ q x := by
      filter_upwards [f] with x hx using Or.inl hp
    exact h₁
  | inr hq =>
    -- Case: ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x is true
    have h₁ : ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p ∨ q x := by
      filter_upwards [hq] with x hx using Or.inr hx
    exact h₁

have h_main : (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p ∨ q x) ↔ p ∨ ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x := by
  constructor
  · -- Prove the forward direction: (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p ∨ q x) → p ∨ ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x
    intro h
    exact h_main_forward h
  · -- Prove the backward direction: p ∨ ∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, q x → (∀ᶠ (x : α) in f, p ∨ q x)
    intro h
    exact h_main_backward h

script:
intro α s t
intro h₁ h₂ h₃
have h₄ : ∃ (x : α), s = {x} ∧ t = {x} := by
  -- We need to show that there exists an element `x` such that `s = {x}` and `t = {x}`.
  -- First, we use the fact that `s ×ˢ t ⊆ SetRel.id` to deduce properties about `s` and `t`.
  have h₅ : s.Nonempty := h₁
  have h₆ : t.Nonempty := h₂
  have h₇ : s ×ˢ t ⊆ SetRel.id := h₃
  -- Since `s ×ˢ t ⊆ SetRel.id`, it means that for any `(a, b) ∈ s ×ˢ t`, we must have `a = b`.
  -- We can use this to show that all elements in `s` and `t` are the same.
  obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := h₅
  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := h₆
  have h₈ : (x, y) ∈ s ×ˢ t := by
    exact ⟨hx, hy⟩
  have h₉ : (x, y) ∈ SetRel.id := h₇ h₈
  have h₁₀ : x = y := by simpa [SetRel.id] using h₉
  -- Now we need to show that `s` and `t` are singletons.
  have h₁₁ : s = {x} := by
    apply Set.ext
    intro a
    constructor
    · -- Prove the forward direction: if `a ∈ s`, then `a = x`.
      intro ha
      have h₁₂ : (a, y) ∈ s ×ˢ t := by
        exact ⟨ha, hy⟩
      have h₁₃ : (a, y) ∈ SetRel.id := h₇ h₁₂
      have h₁₄ : a = y := by simpa [SetRel.id] using h₁₃
      have h₁₅ : a = x := by rw [h₁₀] at *; exact h₁₄
      exact h₁₅
    · -- Prove the reverse direction: if `a = x`, then `a ∈ s`.
      intro ha
      rw [ha]
      exact hx
  have h₁₂ : t = {x} := by
    apply Set.ext
    intro b
    constructor
    · -- Prove the forward direction: if `b ∈ t`, then `b = x`.
      intro hb
      have h₁₃ : (y, b) ∈ s ×ˢ t := by
        exact ⟨hy, hb⟩
      have h₁₄ : (y, b) ∈ SetRel.id := h₇ h₁₃
      have h₁₅ : y = b := by simpa [SetRel.id] using h₁₄
      have h₁₆ : b = x := by rw [h₁₀] at *; exact h₁₅.symm
      exact h₁₆
    · -- Prove the reverse direction: if `b = x`, then `b ∈ t`.
      intro hb
      rw [hb]
      have h₁₃ : y = x := by rw [h₁₀]
      rw [h₁₃] at hy
      exact hy
  -- Finally, we need to find an element `x` such that `s = {x}` and `t = {x}`.
  refine' ⟨x, _⟩
  constructor
  · -- Prove `s = {x}`.
    exact h₁₁
  · -- Prove `t = {x}`.
    exact h₁₂
